title: From Cells to Organs
objective: After this level you can explain how cells form tissues, organs and whole systems.
summary: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form systems. The four tissue types are epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous, and the stomach wall uses all four.

cards.headline: Your stomach isn't made of 'stomach'.
cards.body: Its wall is a lining, packing, muscle and nerves: four different tissues stacked into one organ. Every organ is built from tissues like that. Here's the ladder from a single cell to a whole working body.

cards.headline: Cells, tissues, organs, systems, you
cards.body: Your body is built in levels. A tissue is a group of similar cells working together on one job. An organ is a distinct structure made of two or more tissue types. An organ system is a group of organs teaming up on a major job, and your 11 systems together make the whole organism: you. Each rung of the ladder is built from the one below it.

items.label: Cover and hold
points: Epithelial: sheets that cover surfaces and line passages

items.label: Move and signal
points: Nervous: sends signals between body parts

cards.headline: The stomach, layer by layer
cards.body: Back to that stomach. Inside is an epithelial lining. Around it, connective tissue holds the layers together. Then come three layers of smooth muscle that churn food, with networks of nerves running through the wall. Four tissue types, one organ, and that organ is one member of the digestive system you met in Level 1.

cards.headline: The ladder: climbed
learned: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs
Four tissue types: epithelial, connective, muscle, nervous
The stomach wall uses all four

questions.prompt: Which tissue type covers the body's surfaces and lines its inner passages?

options.label: Connective
options.rationale: Connective tissue binds, supports and protects.

questions.explanation: Epithelial tissue forms sheets that cover surfaces and line passages.

questions.prompt: Put the body's building levels in order. Which list runs from smallest to largest?

options.label: Tissue, cell, organ, organ system
options.rationale: Tissues are made of cells, so cells come first.

options.label: Organ, tissue, cell, organ system
options.rationale: Organs are made of tissues, not the reverse.

questions.explanation: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs form organ systems.

questions.prompt: Where does the stomach fit in the levels of the body you have met so far?

options.label: It is an organ, part of the digestive system
It is a single tissue made of one cell type
options.rationale: Its wall has four tissue types.

options.label: It is a whole organ system on its own
options.rationale: It is one member of the digestive system.

options.label: It is one giant cell
options.rationale: It is built from many tissues, each made of many cells.

questions.explanation: The stomach is an organ made of four tissue types, and it belongs to the digestive system.
